metadata.title: SpaceX stock has rocky week ahead of earnings

content.text:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock whipsawed through a volatile week, swinging from an all-time low to a sharp rebound and back again, as investors brace for the newly public company's first earnings report and a major share unlock.
Shares were mostly flat in early trade on Friday, steadying after a rough stretch. The stock hit an all-time low of $109.53 on Monday before closing down 1.4% at $113.50, then rebounded 2.6% on Tuesday, only to come back under pressure midweek. For the week, the stock is down around 5%.
SpaceX shares have shed nearly 30% from their $150 market debut last month, and remain down roughly 50% from their all-time high of $225.64.
The swings come ahead of SpaceX's second quarter earnings, due Aug. 4. But a bigger overhang is a lockup expiration on Aug. 6 that will free as much as 20% of shares for sale under the company's lockup plan. Many investors worry the added supply will keep the stock under pressure.
In addition, CEO Elon Musk is still reportedly pushing for a merger of SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA). The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that executives are trying to decide how to dispose of Tesla's China business in the event of a merger. SpaceX's government and national defense contracts could be a concern for the Chinese government.
"A potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla would likely trigger intense scrutiny from Beijing, given that a major U.S. defense contractor would control Tesla's factories in China and the factories' know-how and supply chain could be repurposed for the U.S. military," the Journal reported sources saying.
Another concern for China would be SpaceX (and potentially the US government) getting data from China's two million Tesla owners, sources told the Journal.
Merger talk aside, when SpaceX reports results next week investors will have a close eye on SpaceX's capex investments, S&P Global Visible Alpha analyst Melissa Otto wrote.
"SpaceX's capex numbers are expected to increase from $48.7 billion this year to $118.4 billion in FY 2028… In addition, SpaceX's overall debt is also projected to grow over 5x from $41.7 billion this year to over $218.0 billion in FY 2028," Otto noted.
The concern with SpaceX's big capital requirements — like those of the large AI frontier startups and even Oracle (ORCL), Alphabet (GOOGL), and Meta (META) — is that its AI infrastructure investments will not be able to generate a healthy return given the level of cash needed.
Pras Subramanian is Lead Transportation Reporter for Yahoo Finance. You can follow him on X and on Instagram.
